title_ar: فضيلة الشيخ يحاضر في دولة الكويت الشقيقة
title_en: His Eminence the Sheikh lectures in the sisterly State of Kuwait
body_ar:
ضمن الأنشطة العلمية التي يقوم بها فضيلة العلامة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو هذه الأيام بدولة الكويت الشقيقة، قدم الشيخ مجموعة محاضرات في إطار برنامج ثقافي وعلمي تستضيفه جامعة الكويت بالتعاون مع وزارة الأوقاف الكويتية، وقد قدم الشيخ لحد الآن سبع محاضرات؛ اثنتان منها ضمن دورة الأصول المقدمة لأساتذة وطلاب كلية الشريعة في جامعة الكويت.

واثنتان ضمن دورة القواعد الفقهية الكبرى، التي تنظمها وزارة الأوقاف في مدينة الجهراء، ومحاضرتان لدكتورات وطالبات الدراسات العليا بجامعة الكويت الأولى، بعنوان: "منهجية التعامل مع مستجدات العصر"، والثانية بعنوان: "أثر العرف والعادة في الفتاوى المتعلقة بالمرأة"، أما المحاضرة السابعة فقد قدمها الشيخ في أحد مساجد العاصمة "الكويت" تحت عنوان: "دور الفرد المسلم في بناء المجتمع"، وما يزال برنامج الشيخ مستمرا حتى مساء الأربعاء، حيث سيكمل دورتيْ: الأصول والقواعد، كما سيقدم محاضرة أخرى لطالبات جامعة الكويت غدا تحت عنوان: "الليونة والتضييق في الفتوى".
body_en:
As part of the scholarly activities which his eminence the erudite Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew is undertaking these days in the sisterly State of Kuwait, the Sheikh has delivered a set of lectures within a cultural and scholarly programme hosted by Kuwait University in cooperation with the Kuwaiti Ministry of Endowments. The Sheikh has so far delivered seven lectures, two of them within the course on legal theory given for the teaching staff and students of the Faculty of Sharia at Kuwait University.

Two were within the course on the major legal maxims, organised by the Ministry of Endowments in the city of al-Jahra; and two lectures were for women holding doctorates and for postgraduate women students at Kuwait University — the first entitled "A Method for Dealing with the Newly Arisen Questions of the Age", and the second entitled "The Effect of Custom and Usage on Fatwas Relating to Women". The seventh lecture the Sheikh delivered in one of the mosques of the capital, Kuwait City, under the title "The Role of the Individual Muslim in Building Society". The Sheikh's programme continues until Wednesday evening, when he will complete the two courses on legal theory and on the maxims; he will also deliver a further lecture tomorrow to the women students of Kuwait University, entitled "Latitude and Strictness in Issuing a Fatwa".

options: Latitude and Strictness in Issuing a Fatwa
Leniency and Restriction in the Fatwa
Flexibility and Narrowing in Legal Opinion
flags.note: A lecture title, so a fixed rendering matters for cross-referencing against the audio archive. Līnah/luyūnah is softness or pliancy; taḍyīq is the narrowing or tightening of what is allowed. Option 0 reads best in English but 'latitude' is an interpretation. The Sheikh's office may already have an English title for this lecture, which should take precedence.

flags.note: CRITICAL FOR DISPLAY, in combination with the date problem. The item says 'tomorrow' and 'until Wednesday evening'. The only date the CMS gives is 27 December 2010, which is a bulk-upload timestamp for this whole range and not necessarily the day the notice was written, so the references cannot be resolved with confidence. Option 1 would fix dates that the record does not actually establish. The related announcement at id 546, already in the corpus, dates the Kuwait lecture series to 26–29 December 2010, which is consistent but is not proof for this item.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.
The date shown by the CMS is a bulk-upload timestamp shared by every item in this range, not the date the Sheikh gave the answer. The real date of composition is unknown. See date_is_cms_bulk_upload.
This is a site news notice, not a fatwa or a teaching text, and is typed 'news' for that reason.

'The sisterly State of Kuwait' renders dawlat al-Kuwayt al-shaqīqah, the conventional Arabic formula between Arab states. It has been kept rather than flattened to 'Kuwait', since it is part of the register of the notice.
'The erudite' renders al-ʿallāmah, an honorific for a scholar of wide learning.
'Ministry of Endowments' renders wizārat al-awqāf, the standard name of the ministry; waqf here is the institution of the religious endowment, not an individual endowment.
The lecture titles are given in quotation marks in the source and are rendered as titles, not as descriptions of content.
